newsitem.title: UK: European markets subdued before US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: European markets subdued before US jobs data.

text.p: European financial markets were subdued on Friday morning, with operators little inclined to go out on a limb ahead of crucial U.S. jobs data due at 1230 GMT.
Most European stock markets were slightly lower, depressed by a fall on Wall Street overnight, while the dollar was steady.
"It is very quiet with maybe a little bit of position squaring," said Peter Wood, a currency dealer at Bank of Boston in London. "We can't see anyone doing too much ahead of the figures."

The dollar was given a boost on Thursday by news of a reduction in the Japanese trade deficit as well as "safe haven" buying after the announcement that Russian President Boris Yeltsin was to have a heart operation.
By midsession on Friday, it was quoted at 109.20 yen, barely changed from the 109.10 European close on Thursday.
Average forecasts point to a rise of 244,000 in the U.S. August non-farm payroll after a rise of 193,000 in July.
"A strong figure has been priced into the market to a degree, but if it's up to 300,000 then it could start to worry," said Wood at the Bank of Boston.
A strong jobs figure could raise worries about the economy overheating and prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next policy meeting on September 24.

U.S. markets had a foretaste of the figures on Thursday when the Labor Department reported that new applications for unemployment benefits fell by an unexpectedly sharp 15,000 last week, ending four straight weeks of rises.
U.S. Treasury bonds fell on the report and the Dow Jones Average on Wall Street lost 49.94 points to 5,606.96.
There was a knock-on effect in London, where shares were marked down at the opening, but news of a 0.5 percent increase in manufacturing output in July helped steady the market.
However, volume was minimal. "Our market seems to be distancing itself from Wall Street somewhat," said one head trader, "but no-one really wants to take a punt ahead of the figures."
At 1045 GMT the FTSE index of 100 top London shares was down 22 points at 3,865.2.
In Paris, French stocks were down 7.55 points at 1,988.68 in similarly thin trading ahead of the U.S. figures.

On Thursday, the French government unveiled details of income tax cuts plus higher taxes on tobacco and alcohol. It forecast that economic growth would rise to 2.3 percent in 1997 from a forecast 1.3 percent this year.
One trader said the market was generally pleased with the French government's tax cut proposals "but the U.S. jobs figure will probably have a bigger impact".
The franc, weak of late due to worries about industrial unrest as the government imposes a tight budget, was steady at 3.4225 per mark.
Worries about how the Spanish government will cut its budget deficit hurt the Madrid bourse, which was down around 0.70 percent at midsession.
German shares were undermined by Wall Street and the 30-share DAX index was down 13.21 points at 2,516.33.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4845 marks and 109.15 yen, barely changed from 1.4850 and 109.10 on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 22 points at 3,865.2.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was down 13.21 points at 2,516.33.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 7.55 points at 1,988.68.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $385.60 against $386.35 at the close on Thursday. Silver was off five cents at $5.15.
